message.text: `probingHost` adds only the kind of the macOS git lookup (`linked` or `linked-no-system`) to the probing host. It leaves out which git program the probe runs and what version it is. The test in probing-level.test.ts even asserts that moving git's paths alone reuses the run.

evidence.snippet: The host gains one field, `sandboxVersion`, the installed release of sandbox-runtime, which `probingHost` reads from the package's own `package.json`, as the Pi versions are read. A release of the sandbox can change what a probe may do, so a review after an upgrade runs each probing lens again. A test's own sandbox reports the installed release too.

Choice: every run's selection, the first and the one a quick run escalates to, names its whole probing environment as one JSON value, so any change to its writer, the policy's word, its time limit, its grant or its host runs it again. The host is one value: the sandbox's platform and kind, and the CPU architecture and version of the Node that runs the probes. The coordinator chose that on 2026-11-14, applying the shared-record decision the maintainer adopted on 2026-11-13, that a check's request holds its host facts. The probing protocol also holds what Melian's probe runner gives a probe, over fixed paths, which the coordinator chose on 2026-11-14 under the same decision. [The identity guideline](../guidelines/identity.md) lists what about the host and the runner is left out, and why. The planner's decisions at base and its earlier findings leave the instruction fingerprint, as the caller-context decision kept caller context out, and stay in the prompt. That exclusion was a builder's choice; the maintainer accepted it on 2026-11-13, in the coordinator's session, after a host round at `4f83a8a6` raised it. The fingerprint holds the probing protocol as the build renders it, so a Melian release that changes it runs the level again: each role tool's name, description and schema, the fixed limits, and the table of every fixed wording the planner and the prober read, the planner's role and context among them. The prompt functions build their text from that table and hold no wording of their own, so every branch of each counts, and a test fails when one does. The verifier's version hashes the wording it reads of a claim's probe, a table of its own, the same way. Beside each table, each key hashes its prompts as `probingRenderings` renders them over fixed samples, one for each branch the render functions hold, so a change in how a prompt is put together, its order, separators or quoting, runs the level again or judges stored claims again. explanation.what: `probingHost` adds only the kind of the macOS git lookup (`linked` or `linked-no-system`) to the probing host. It leaves out which git program the probe runs and what version it is. The test in probing-level.test.ts even asserts that moving git's paths alone reuses the run.
explanation.whatToDo: Add git's version to `probingHost` next to the kind, e.g. by asking the chosen program `--version` with the same cleaned environment in `probeGit` and carrying it on the `linked` answer. Keep it absent where git is unavailable or on Linux, so earlier keys still hold. Or put the omission to the maintainer, as was done for the node_modules reinstall gap, instead of the coordinator choosing it.
explanation.whyHere: The base probing decisions key a host tool whose release can change a probe's answer: Node's version, and since 2026-11-16 sandbox-runtime's release ("A release of the sandbox can change what a probe may do, so a review after an upgrade runs each probing lens again"). The attach-key decision says any change to the run's grant or its host runs it again. This change makes git a tool probes run, and its stated purpose is probes that run `git` and the `melian` CLI on top of it. Yet a different git from the developer tools leaves the key as it was. The decision's reason is that the paths name the host's install. That covers the path, but not the version, which the key could hold as cheaply as Node's.

properties.failureScenario: A reviewer on macOS reviews a head with the probing level. `xcode-select -p` names /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools, and its Apple Git 2.4x runs in the probe. The prober runs a probe that drives `melian review` or plain git inside the sandbox, and it ends conclusively (exit 0, clean). The reviewer then updates the Command Line Tools, or runs `xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer`, which ships a different Apple Git release. The system configuration is still present or still absent, so `probingHost` still returns `git: "linked"` with the same platform, sandbox, sandboxVersion, arch and node. The next review of the same head has an unchanged lens request, so `runStands` passes and the finished probing run is attached or copied. Its clean result, and the conclusive reruns stored under its probe IDs, stand for a git the probe never ran. A probe that would now fail goes unprobed until the head or another keyed input changes. probing-level.test.ts asserts this outcome: `planned({ program: "/b/usr/bin/git", ... })` returns 0 planner requests.
